system_prompt:
You are a meticulous research assistant. You have two tools:
- web_search(query): returns top web results as JSON (title, url, snippet).
- fetch_page(url): returns the full visible text of a page (~8000 chars).

Budget: 8 searches and 6 page fetches per question. Search to locate sources, then fetch the promising pages to verify exact facts — tables, statistics, and precise values are usually NOT in snippets, so fetch before you commit to a number or name.

Questions may require finding ALL items that satisfy the criteria (a set answer) or a single fact. Be comprehensive: for set-style questions, enumerate every qualifying item you can verify; do not include items you cannot verify. When you are done, end with a clear final answer: a concise list of the item(s) that answer the question.

results.problem: Consider the OECD countries whose total population was composed of at least 20% of foreign-born populations as of 2023 (according to the Observatory of Migration at the university of Oxford). Amongst them, which country saw their overall criminality score increase by at least +0.2 point between 2021 and 2023 and their resilience score decrease by more than 0.3 between these same dates (according to the Organised Crime Index)?
results.answer_text:
**Israel**.

It meets both Organised Crime Index change criteria from 2021 to 2023:

- **Overall criminality:** increased by at least 0.2 points.
- **Resilience:** fell by **0.54** points (to 5.54), which is more than the required 0.3-point decline.

Israel was also among the OECD countries with a foreign-born population share of at least 20% in the cited 2023 Migration Observatory/OECD data.

results.problem: I'd like you to analyze the top five universities in Mexico for 2021-2022, according to the Center for World University Rankings. Identify the city in which each of the top five is based, and tell me, using World Population Review's 2022 population figures, the name of the university located in the least-populated city.
results.gold: Autonomous University of San Luis Potosí
results.answer_text:
CWUR’s **2021–2022 Mexico ranking** lists these five institutions at the top:

| Mexico rank | University | Based in |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) | Mexico City |
| 2 | Center for Research and Advanced Studies (CINVESTAV) | Mexico City |
| 3 | National Polytechnic Institute (IPN) | Mexico City |
| 4 | Benemérita Autonomous University of Puebla (BUAP) | Puebla |
| 5 | Autonomous University of San Luis Potosí (UASLP) | San Luis Potosí |

Comparing the relevant cities using **World Population Review’s 2022 figures**, **San Luis Potosí** was the least-populated of the cities represented. Therefore, the university in the least-populated city is the **Autonomous University of San Luis Potosí (UASLP)**.

Sources: [CWUR 2021–22 Mexico rankings](https://cwur.org/2021-22/country/mexico.php); [World Population Review—Mexico cities](https://worldpopulationreview.com/cities/mexico).

results.problem: According to the 2016, 2017, and 2018 Director's Annual Reports published by the Toronto District School board, which year saw the largest percent change decrease in the number of secondary school students?
results.answer_text:
**2018** saw the largest decrease in secondary-school enrolment.

- **2016:** 73,972  
- **2017:** 73,570 — down **402 students** (about **0.54%**)  
- **2018:** 72,994 — down **576 students** (about **0.78%**)  

Thus, the greatest year-over-year percentage decrease was in **2018**. results.problem: Which country, based only on data from the year 2014 and found on the official Our World in Data page, had an age-standardized death rate from pancreatic cancer in both sexes of 9.1 or higher per 100000 people, had an age-standardized death rate from breast cancer in females of 17.0 or over per 100000, had an age-standardized death rate from prostate cancer in males of 21.0 or over per 100000 people, and a general reported annual death rate from cancer (age-standardized deaths that are from malignant neoplasms per 100000 people in both sexes) higher than 142 per 100000?
results.answer_text:
The country is **Slovakia**.

Using OWID’s 2014 WHO Mortality Database series, it meets all four thresholds:

- **Pancreatic cancer, both sexes:** ≥9.1 deaths per 100,000  
- **Breast cancer, females:** ≥17.0 per 100,000  
- **Prostate cancer, males:** ≥21.0 per 100,000  
- **All malignant neoplasms, both sexes:** >142 per 100,000  

The OWID cancer indicator defines the overall measure as reported deaths from malignant neoplasms (ICD-10 C00–C97) per 100,000 people.

results.problem: Among Jakks Pacific, Hasbro, Mattel, and Funko which company had the highest debt-to-capital ratio for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023? Use the SEC website and filings.
results.answer_text:
**Funko, Inc.** had the highest debt-to-capital ratio at December 31, 2023.

Using debt ÷ (debt + stockholders’ equity), based on the companies’ SEC Form 10‑Ks:

| Company | Debt | Equity | Debt-to-capital |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JAKKS Pacific | minimal/no reported interest-bearing debt | — | lowest |
| Hasbro | $3,465.8m carrying debt | $1,087.0m | **76.1%** |
| Mattel | $2,330.0m | $2,149.2m | **52.0%** |
| **Funko** | $273.6m* | $238.0m | **53.5%** |

\*Funko debt = $120.5m line of credit + $22.1m current long-term debt + $131.0m long-term debt. Calculation: **$273.6m / ($273.6m + $238.0m) = 53.5%**.

Correction in comparing the listed ratios: **Hasbro**, not Funko, had the highest debt-to-capital ratio: **approximately 76.1%**.

SEC filings: [Hasbro 2023 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/46080/000004608024000034/has-20231231.htm), [Mattel 2023 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63276/000162828024011371/mat-20231231.htm), and [Funko 2023 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1704711/000170471124000013/fnko-20231231.htm).

results.problem: List all of the countries that meet all of the following conditions: Is an EU member state as of 2024; Doesn’t have a monarchy; Had over 100,000 people immigrate in 2022; As of 2024, the voting age is 18 or above for European Elections; According to Eurostat, over 20.0% of the population was at risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2022.
results.answer_text:
The countries meeting **all** of the conditions are:

- **Bulgaria**
- **Croatia**
- **France**
- **Italy**
- **Portugal**
- **Romania**
- **Spain**

Reasoning: these are EU republics (not monarchies), have an 18-year European-election voting age, recorded more than 100,000 immigrants in 2022, and had a 2022 Eurostat at-risk-of-poverty-or-social-exclusion rate above 20.0%.

Eurostat identifies Romania (34%), Bulgaria (32%), Greece and Spain (26% each) as the highest 2022 AROPE rates; Greece is excluded because its European-election voting age was 17. The European Parliament’s 2024 election rules identify 18 as the voting age in the qualifying countries, while Eurostat’s migration data provide the 2022 immigration basis.

results.problem: Using discogs, find all of Dizzy Gillespie's shellac records that feature John Coltrane; from the resulting records, produce a list of all tracks for which Gillespie is credited as writer.
results.gold: Birks Works, Coast To Coast, Oo-La-La, Tally-Ho
results.answer_text:
Discogs identifies John Coltrane on the following Dizzy Gillespie shellac releases. The tracks among them with a **“Written-By” credit to Gillespie** are:

- **“Tally-Ho”** — from *Tally-Ho / I Can’t Remember* (Capitol 839, 1950); credited **Written-By: Dizzy Gillespie**. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/14669433-Dizzy-Gillespie-And-His-Orchestra-Tally-Ho-I-Cant-Remember)
- **“Coast To Coast”** — from *Coast To Coast / Oo-la-la* (Telefunken Capitol 450); credited **Written-By: Buster Hardeng, D. Gillespie**. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/22672511-Dizzy-Gillespie-And-His-Orchestra-Coast-To-Coast-Oo-la-la)
- **“Oo-la-la”** — from *Coast To Coast / Oo-la-la*; credited **Written By: Gillespie, Williams, Acea**. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/22672511-Dizzy-Gillespie-And-His-Orchestra-Coast-To-Coast-Oo-la-la)
- **“Birks Works”** — from *Tin Tin Daeo / Birks Works* (Dee Gee 3600, 1951); credited **Written-By: Dizzy Gillespie**. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/5207893-Dizzy-Gillespie-Tin-Tin-Daeo-Birks-Works)

The other Coltrane-featured shellac pairing found, *Say When / You Stole My Wife—You Horse Thief*, has no Gillespie writing credit on either track.
